cards.text: David is king, and a delivery shows up from Hiram, king of Tyre. Envoys, cedar logs, stonemasons AND carpenters. Friend, that's not a gift basket, that's a whole construction crew.

cards.question: Hiram's stonemasons and carpenters roll in with cedar logs. What did Hiram send them to build for David?

cards.text: Then David realizes something big about his kingdom.

cards.question: David realizes the ___ has made him king over Israel and lifted his kingdom high for the sake of His ___.

cards.text: In Jerusalem, David takes more wives and has more sons and daughters, and the list of children born there runs thirteen names long, Solomon included. THIRTEEN, friend, and I thought six cookie cutters made a crowded counter.
The Philistines hear David's been anointed king over all Israel, and they all go out searching for him. And trust me, friend, these folks are NOT bringing cedar logs.

cards.question: David learns the Philistines are searching for him, so he hides until they give up and go home.

cards.text: The Philistines come and raid the Valley of Rephaim. Before David goes up against them, there's something he does first.

cards.question: The Philistines are raiding the Valley of Rephaim. What does David do before he goes up against them?

answers.text: He asks God what to do
He sends gifts to make peace

cards.question: When David asks, the LORD tells him to go and promises to deliver the Philistines into his hand.

cards.text: So David and his men go up to Baal-perazim, and David defeats the Philistines. Just like God said, JUST like He said.

cards.question: After the win at Baal-perazim, David gives the credit to the courage of his men.

cards.text: David says, “Like a bursting flood, God has burst out against my enemies by my hand.” Then the Philistines leave something behind there, something they should NEVER leave behind.

cards.question: The Philistines flee Baal-perazim and leave something behind. What do they abandon there?
The Philistines left their gods behind at Baal-perazim. What does David order done with them?

cards.text: But the Philistines aren't done, and once again they raid the valley. It's the snooze button all over again: you KNOW it's coming back.

cards.question: With the Philistines back in the valley, David skips asking God this time, since he already won once.

cards.text: David asks God again, and God answers. But this time, the plan is different.

cards.question: God gives David a new plan for the second Philistine raid. What is it?

answers.text: Circle around to the balsam trees
Wait for them back in Jerusalem

cards.text: Then God gives David a signal, up in the tops of the balsam trees. The second he hears it, he moves out to battle.

cards.question: David's signal to move out is the sound of ___ in the tops of the balsam trees.
When David hears marching in the tops of the balsam trees, what does God say it will mean?

answers.text: God has gone out ahead of him
His army is ready to fight

cards.text: So David does exactly as God commanded him. Friend, when the signal is coming from the TREETOPS, you do not freestyle.

cards.question: Following God's plan, David's men strike down the Philistine army all the way from ___ to ___.

cards.text: And after all that, David's fame goes out into every land. Every. Single. One.

cards.question: As David's fame spreads, all the nations come to fear him. Who causes that?

findings.problem: This story card is just 'Then David realizes something big about his kingdom.' It has no Papa Dorin voice, and it gives the baker nothing to reason with before the fill-in-the-blank about who made David king and for whose sake.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question capitalizes the pronoun in 'for the sake of His ___'. That marks the subject of the first blank as divine, so 'Hiram' is ruled out for blank 1 before the baker reasons at all, and 'LORD' stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This is the first time the Philistines appear, and Papa Dorin never says who they are. He could say, for example, that they are a people David calls his enemies (1 Chronicles 14:11).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'The second he hears it, he moves out to battle' reads as if it is already happening. In 1 Chronicles 14:15 it is God's instruction to David, and David only carries it out in 14:16. The card should frame it as what God tells him to do.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Carried back to Jerusalem' is false in this passage. But the parallel account in 2 Samuel 5:21 says David and his men carried the Philistine idols away, so a baker who knows that passage could argue for it.
findings.question: The rule says a wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, and a wrong answer a baker could argue is right gets replaced. Does that reach parallel accounts in other books, like 2 Samuel 5 for 1 Chronicles 14, so wrong answers must also be false there?
